text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and uveitis, does the ulcer have a raised, violaceous border that appears to spread in a serpiginous pattern? I also need to know if you have experienced any recent joint pain or eye redness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of an insect bite followed by a painful ulcer with purplish, irregular borders and central necrosis is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum, especially given your underlying Crohn's disease.
